findings.explanation: The new IssueBulkUpdateDateEndpoint.post performs a bulk update of issue start_date/target_date. The @allow_permission([ROLE.ADMIN, ROLE.MEMBER]) decorator (base.py:14-59) only verifies the requester is an active member of the project identified by kwargs['slug']/kwargs['project_id']. It does not verify that the issues being updated actually belong to that project. The changed code fetches issues by user-supplied IDs with no workspace/project scoping: `issues = list(Issue.objects.filter(id__in=issue_ids))` and then `Issue.objects.bulk_update(issues_to_update, ['start_date','target_date'])`. A user with MEMBER role in project A can therefore modify the dates of issues that belong to any other project (e.g. project B where they have no role) by supplying those issues' UUIDs. This is an IDOR: the object is fetched by user-controlled identifier without verifying the requester owns it / is allowed to access it.
